deviations_from_card: Commit order: the refactor lands first and MetricTest second, because MetricTest cannot compile before Metric exists; red-before was measured in the working tree against today's API (pick without a metric): 6 of 7 MetricTest cases red, case 2 green (guard), case 8 is the existing suite (guard, green before and after). The card's cases say 'aspect = 16/9'; per the critic the parameter is a Metric, so tests pass Metric(16.0 / 9.0). HitTest.pointToSegment moved to Metric.pointToSegment; the existing pure-geometry pointToSegment case in HitTestTest now calls Metric(1.0).pointToSegment with its values unchanged (0.1 and 0.2). Smoothing.path also gained a Metric parameter (it calls decimate; it has no callers). The decimation threshold became Smoothing.MIN_POINT_DISTANCE so Overlay references it instead of copying it. :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest not run: tv-app has no src/test. No desk/ or tools/ touched, so no desk gate.
notes: For pen-core B (wave 2), the new signatures: data class Metric(val aspect: Double) in core/Metric.kt (require aspect finite and > 0) with distance(ax, ay, bx, by), distance(a: List<Double>, b: List<Double>), pointToSegment(px, py, ax, ay, bx, by), apart(a, b, minDistance): Boolean, all in content-width units (y divided by aspect). HitTest.pick(annotations, x, y, metric: Metric, tolerance = DEFAULT_TOLERANCE) and HitTest.distanceTo(a, x, y, metric); HitTest.pointToSegment is gone (use Metric). Smoothing.decimate(points, metric: Metric, minDistance = MIN_POINT_DISTANCE), Smoothing.path(points, metric, tension = 1.0), const Smoothing.MIN_POINT_DISTANCE = 0.004. PenEngine: a new `private val metric = Metric(videoAspect)` right after overrideHoldMs; the private distance() helper is removed; handleShape uses metric.distance, handleErase passes metric to pick, the 'up' branch passes metric to decimate. accept()'s when-block (Clear/Undo/Redo) is untouched. Protocol.kt: only a KDoc line on Erase.tolerance. Overlay StrokeRender decimates in pixels (dx*rect.width, dy*rect.height vs rect.w(MIN_POINT_DISTANCE)). No wire or schema change. No device available: the drawn ring size and eraser reach on the TV are proven by JVM tests and ContentRect arithmetic only, not seen on screen. companion/index.html:388 already previews circles with a pixel hypot, so the phone and TV should now agree - unverified on a device.
